name: Alert
summary: Inline message that stays in context.

a11y.apg: The APG pattern is Alert. `danger` renders role="alert", which interrupts the screen reader; the other three render role="status", which waits for a pause. No keyboard interaction: an Alert is read, not operated — one that can be dismissed is a Banner.

props.name: variant
props.description: Tone and, with it, the live region: `danger` renders role="alert", which interrupts the screen reader; the other three render role="status", which waits for a pause. Colour is never the only signal — what carries the meaning is the text.

props.name: title
props.description: Rendered as a <strong> above the body. Optional on purpose: a one-line alert reads better without one.

props.name: children
props.description: The message. An Alert stays in the reading flow, in context — a page-width warning is a Banner and a transient one is a Toast.

props.name: state
props.type: waiting_user | waiting_approval | waiting_dependency | offline | stale | partial | degraded
props.description: Universal state (Part J) — an axis of its own alongside `variant`, because the two answer different questions: `variant` is how serious this is, `state` is what is happening. Merging them would put “out of date” next to “danger” and force the caller to pick one. It sets `data-state`, derives the severity when no `variant` is given — waiting states inform, the rest warn, and none of the seven is `danger`, because in all seven the screen still works — and supplies the message when there are no children.

props.name: icon
props.description: Overrides the glyph. The icon is a FUNCTION of the variant by default, because a system that makes you remember which glyph means "danger" ends up with four answers to the same question.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Adds the close button on the third track of the grid. Without it that track holds an empty span, so the body keeps the same width either way.
